<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fb6fb24e2ffb2fee0cd94d7acaf7030a780e179d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5d3e07a47f3a9e717af470ee4f818fd0357b9f17 && git checkout 5d3e07a47f3a9e717af470ee4f818fd0357b9f17
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fb6fb24e2ffb2fee0cd94d7acaf7030a780e179d` → pass the list as

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · `domain:services` seat 1 (#6021) · `marchtian` · `session_01Nk17Z26X5DB59iQztDBADH` · 2026-10-18T05:39Z · head `dc1de5306f`. The seat's own review at `TIER_DEFAULT`: `--tier` read no path-derived mandate, and the diff touches no published schema or governed text. It lands through the merge queue once every check on this head is green.

- **Shape:** a draft PR to `main`. Its first line is `Fixes #24235`, and that is the only closing keyword in the body. `Clause-②: no` is at a line start in the body and in the changeset (`@objectstack/plugin-audit` patch). Card and PR assignee: `marchtian`. Not governed: `check-governed-merges` reads none of the 4 paths, and 286 changed lines ≤ 3000.
- **The premise, measured before the fix:** on `main` `f5ef054a7`, with a real kernel and the real `SettingsService`, the audited write right after `localization.locale` was set to `zh-CN` stored the English line. The same write on this branch stores the Chinese one.
- **The fix, read by the seat in `audit-writers.ts`:**
  - One rule retires a held write locale. Each entry is stamped with a generation, read before the lookup, and an entry with an older stamp is dead. A settings write that lands while a lookup is in flight therefore leaves the pre-write answer unheld.
  - The writer's own `afterInsert` / `afterUpdate` / `afterDelete` hooks advance the generation, scoped to `sys_setting` and `sys_platform_setting`. They carry the writer's `packageId`, so `unregisterHooksByPackage` still clears them on a hot reload. The handler re-checks `ctx.object`.
  - `SettingsService` persists through the engine, so a change made through the settings API is such a write, and so is a seeder's direct row write. The seat confirmed that only `service-settings` writes either store in `packages/**` source, so nothing writes them on a request's hot path, and the coarse any-namespace retirement costs one locale read per scope.
  - The 30 s TTL now bounds only what the hooks cannot see. Host-first precedence is untouched: `audit-plugin.ts` is not in the diff.
- **Pins:** `audit-write-locale-settings-seam.integration.test.ts` runs on a real engine with the clock frozen, so no case passes by the TTL. An insert and then an update of the setting each reach the very next audited write (`创建了 Task "T3"`, `Task「T4」を作成しました`). The control writes read the settings store 0 times. Two cases in `audit-writers.test.ts` cover both stores and the in-flight write. The dev's ablation (dropping the generation check) turned 3 cases red with the pin's own message, and the restore is blob-equal to HEAD.
- **Gates on this head:** 34 checks succeeded and 6 were skipped by design (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance: the roster set). There were no failures, and the required contexts are green. Locally the dev derived 68 families on this head, ran all 68, and all exited 0 (`--ran`: 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN).
- **Accepted deviations:**
  - **The suggested route was measured and not taken.** Every audited write moves the engine epoch before the after-hook asks. So reading through the core resolver with no memo, or retiring on the epoch, costs 2 settings reads on every audited write. Retiring on writes to the two stores is the card's Wanted ("the same seam that retires the core resolver"), spelled at the writer.
  - **The permanent pin uses a stand-in `sys_setting`.** `plugin-audit` has no `service-settings` dependency, and adding one is outside the claim. The real-`SettingsService` reading was a one-off and is in the PR body.
  - `origin/main` was merged into the branch (`8eccf519d`), with no overlap with the diff. Tests and all 68 gates were re-run on the merge head.
- **Out-of-scope findings, with their carriers:**
  - Two `packages/core` comments call the writer's staleness harmless and its memo TTL-only: `resolve-authz-context.ts:1795`–`:1798` and `resolve-authz-context.test.ts:422`–`:428`. Carrier: the `domain:engine` seat, on its next touch of that file. The seat notes it on #6367 at landing.
  - Acceptance notes: a `localization` write on another node, and a host `getLocale` resolver's own storage, stay bounded by the 30 s TTL. The writer does not subscribe to the remote invalidation bridge. That residual is narrower than the card's p3 window and no user has reached it.
